numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When converting from CylindricalRepresentation to PhysicsSphericalRepresentation for vectors very close to the Z axis, the computed PhysicsSphericalRepresentation.theta was 0 rad instead of a small nonzero value.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: For vectors within milliarcseconds of the Z axis, theta should be computed using arctan2 instead of arccos, producing theta = 1e-08 rad for the shown example.
trigger_conditions: Vector very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds) during CylindricalRepresentation -> PhysicsSphericalRepresentation conversion
Use of the fast-path conversion from CylindricalRepresentation to PhysicsSphericalRepresentation
oracle_clues: The fix changes the computation of theta from np.arccos(self.z / r) to np.arctan2(self.rho, self.z).
The shown before/after outputs define the oracle: theta should be 1.e-08 rad instead of 0. rad for CylindricalRepresentation(1*u.m, 0*u.deg, 1e8*u.m).
Discrepancy occurs for vectors very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds).

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds); specifically exemplified by CylindricalRepresentation(rho=1 m, phi=10 deg, z=1e8 m) producing theta=1e-8 rad instead of 0 rad.
category_specific_evidence: Accuracy bug in CylindricalRepresentation -> PhysicsSphericalRepresentation conversion for vectors very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds), caused by using np.arccos() instead of np.arctan2().
Code change: theta=np.arccos(self.z / r) replaced by theta=np.arctan2(self.rho, self.z) in cylindrical.py represent_as().

Test explicitly covers the small-theta regime: cyl = CylindricalRepresentation(rho=1*u.m, phi=10*u.deg, z=1e8*u.m); got = cyl.represent_as(PhysicsSphericalRepresentation). It then asserts assert_allclose(got.r, 1e8*u.m), assert_allclose(got.phi, 10*u.deg), and assert_allclose(got.theta, 1e-8*u.rad).
Test name/intent: test_to_physicsspherical_small_theta: transformation accurate for small theta.
reproduction_risks: Passages do not specify any dtype or precision (e.g., float32 vs float64) or any numerical-characteristics settings that gate the discrepancy; they only describe the geometry (near Z axis) and show astropy quantities.
Passages do not specify tolerance/rtol/atol behavior; they only use assert_allclose without providing explicit tolerance parameters.
“Within milliarcseconds” is qualitative; only one concrete magnitude example is provided (rho=1 m, z=1e8 m leading to theta=1e-8 rad vs 0 rad).
